we show that the ventral stream of a deep neural network can be wired up in a manner that is consistent with the adult primate ventral stream, with only a tiny fraction of the number of updates that are typically required to train the model on labeled images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adult-like match to the primate visual system is achieved surprisingly quickly and with surprisingly few synaptic updates.

the ventral stream may be surprisingly robust to the precise timing of synaptic updates and that it might be able to achieve adult performance even with a substantial fraction of its synaptic connectivity being randomly distributed.

a surprisingly small amount of supervised training can produce a model with the brain-like ventral stream match, suggesting a potential neuroscientific basis for the surprisingly good performance of deep neural networks in computer vision.
